title.en: Explain apprenticeship, vestibule and internship training

say.en: A woodcutter who never stops to sharpen his saw cuts less and less each day. Training keeps employees sharp. In this lesson: Distinguish training, development and education.
Explain the importance of training.
Explain apprenticeship, vestibule and internship training.

body.en: *Training* increases the knowledge and skills of an employee for a specific job. Development is a wider, career-oriented process of overall growth. Education increases general knowledge and understanding. Training benefits the firm through less wastage, higher productivity, lower turnover and better adaptability, and benefits employees through better careers, higher earnings, safety and satisfaction.

points.en: Benefits to firm and to employees

title.en: On the board: methods of training

narration.en: Watch the board as we build this up step by step.

say.en: Training methods fall into two groups: on the job and off the job.
On the job: learning while doing. Apprenticeship puts a trainee under a master worker.
Internship joins a college and a firm; students learn by working.
Off the job: vestibule training uses similar machines in a separate area.
Others: lectures, films, case studies, computer modelling, programmed instruction.
Remember the triangle: training for the job, development for the career, education for the mind.
Watch the board as we build this up step by step.

narration.en: Match each term to its example.

prompt.en: Match each term to its example.

explanation.en: Training is job-specific, development is career-wide and education is general; apprenticeship, vestibule and internship are three methods of training.

right.en: A cashier learns the new billing software
A manager attends a leadership programme to grow into a senior role
An employee studies economics to widen general understanding
A trainee electrician works under a master electrician for a fixed period
Operators practise on dummy machines in a separate room
An engineering student works in a factory as part of the course

say.en: Match each term to its example.

body.en: Apprenticeship *training*: a trainee works under a master worker for a fixed period, as for plumbers and electricians. Vestibule training: employees learn on similar equipment in a separate area, used when machines are costly or sophisticated. Internship training: a joint programme of educational institutions and firms.

points.en: Apprenticeship: on the job, under a master worker
Vestibule: off the job, separate area, similar equipment

caption.en: Is training worth it? Payback on training cost

narration.en: Training costs money but raises output. Set the cost of training per worker and the extra value each trained worker produces per month to see how fast it pays back.

label.en: Extra output value per worker per month

tryThis.en: At ₹20,000 cost and ₹2,500 extra value a month, how many months to pay back?
Double the extra value: what happens to the payback?
Name two benefits of training that do not show in this number.

say.en: Training costs money but raises output. Set the cost of training per worker and the extra value each trained worker produces per month to see how fast it pays back.

problem.en: A Peenya machine-tool firm buys a costly CNC machine. Training new operators on it directly might damage the machine and stop production. Training costs ₹20,000 per operator and each trained operator adds ₹2,500 of output a month. Suggest a method and find the payback period.

steps.en: Costly, sophisticated machine; avoid disturbing real production: vestibule training on similar equipment in a separate area.
After 8 months, training adds net value every month.

answer.en: Vestibule training; the cost is recovered in 8 months.

narration.en: Let us work through this case together. A Peenya machine-tool firm buys a costly CNC machine. Training new operators on it directly might damage the machine and stop production. Training costs ₹20,000 per operator and each trained operator adds ₹2,500 of output a month. Suggest a method and find the payback period.

say.en: Let us work through this case together. A Peenya machine-tool firm buys a costly CNC machine. Training new operators on it directly might damage the machine and stop production. Training costs 20,000 rupees per operator and each trained operator adds 2,500 rupees of output a month. Suggest a method and find the payback period.
Costly, sophisticated machine; avoid disturbing real production: vestibule training on similar equipment in a separate area.
Payback equals 20,000 rupees divided by 2,500 rupees per month equals 8 months.
After 8 months, training adds net value every month.
So the answer is Vestibule training; the cost is recovered in 8 months.
